name: Inadequate Encryption Strength
principle: The product encrypts sensitive data with a theoretically sound scheme but uses strength parameters too small for the required protection. Short keys, weak groups, or export-grade configurations make brute-force decryption practical with current resources.
detection_signals: Java KeyPairGenerator.initialize(512) or initialize(1024) for RSA/DSA keys protecting sensitive data
Java AlgorithmParameterGenerator.init(512) or init(1024) for Diffie-Hellman parameters
OpenSSL RSA_generate_key_ex(..., bits <= 1024, ...) or EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_rsa_keygen_bits(ctx, bits <= 1024)
OpenSSL DH_generate_parameters_ex(dh, bits <= 1024, ...) or DH parameters with p length <= 1024 bits
TLS configuration string includes EXPORT, EXP, LOW, 40, 56, or cipher suites named TLS_*_EXPORT_*
SSL_CTX_set_tmp_dh() or SSL_CTX_set0_tmp_dh_pkey() uses DH parameters <= 1024 bits
Encryption configuration sets effective key length below 128 bits for sensitive data
negative_signals: RSA key generation uses >= 2048 bits, e.g. KeyPairGenerator.initialize(2048) or EVP_PKEY_CTX_set_rsa_keygen_bits(ctx, 2048)
ECDH/ECDSA uses standard >= 256-bit curves such as secp256r1, secp384r1, or X25519
Diffie-Hellman parameters are >= 2048 bits or use approved named FFDHE groups
TLS configuration disables EXPORT/LOW/40/56 suites and only enables TLS 1.2 strong suites or TLS 1.3
OpenSSL security level enforces adequate strength, e.g. SSL_CTX_set_security_level(ctx, 2) or higher
false_defense_traps: Using a strong algorithm name while configuring a short key or weak group
Allowing weak TLS suites as fallback for legacy clients
Checking only protocol version while leaving export-grade or low-strength cipher suites enabled
Assuming old key-size recommendations remain adequate without periodic cryptographic review
Treating base64, XOR, or custom reversible transforms as encryption
verification_focus: Is sensitive data encrypted with a sound scheme whose key length, group size, or negotiated cipher strength is too small for current brute-force resistance requirements?

consequence_chains.trigger: attacker brute-forces weak encryption protecting stored or transmitted sensitive data
consequence_chains.consequence: confidential application data is decrypted and exposed

consequence_chains.trigger: attacker brute-forces encryption protecting credentials, tokens, or authentication secrets
consequence_chains.consequence: protection mechanism is bypassed and authentication can be defeated

patch_principle: Use encryption schemes and parameter sizes currently considered strong by cryptographic experts and standards bodies.
Use at least 128-bit symmetric strength; use RSA/DH >= 2048 bits or approved ECC curves of >= 256 bits.
Disable export-grade, LOW, 40-bit, 56-bit, and other weak TLS cipher suites and weak fallback paths.
Make cryptographic parameters configurable and periodically upgrade them as recommendations change.
